svg.title: A head injury is a trauma patient first: the primary survey and the Glasgow Coma Scale grade it; a severe injury is acted on for herniation and sent for a STAT CT, which tells epidural, acute subdural, contusion, intracerebral hemorrhage and diffuse axonal injury or traumatic subarachnoid hemorrhage apart, each with its own surgical rule; a concussion is a clinical diagnosis managed by removal, rest and a graded return

svg.text: A airway + C-spine precautions · B breathing · C circulation: large-bore IV, bloods for coagulopathy · D disability: neurological

svg.text: exam + Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) · E expose other injuries

svg.text: GCS grades it: SEVERE 3-8 · MODERATE 9-12 · MILD 13-14 · MINOR 15

svg.text: severe death by admission GCS: over 8 → 12% · 5-7 → 27% · under 5 → 78% · coma over 1 day 30-50% · intracranial
